subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Add fuel to the fire

options.text: Having to start all over again
To make an argument or bad situation worse
A mistake made in something you are trying to achieve
When an attempt fails and it's time to start all over

solution:
The correct answer is "**To make an argument or bad situation worse.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The idiom "add fuel to the fire" means to make a situation worse, especially an argument or conflict.**
 
• किसी स्थिति को बदतर बनाना, विशेषकर बहस या संघर्ष।
 
• The phrase "add fuel" is a metaphor for adding more energy or intensity to a situation that is already heated or intense.
 
• This idiom is often used in a negative context, to criticize someone for making a bad situation even worse.
 
 
• Example: "He added fuel to the fire by insulting her."
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.
